alalal-e93014-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 5: whether and how faith can be great or grow.

alalal-e93014-d1e111.summary: Introduces the question on Lombard's text 'Faith is called great in cognition...'.

alalal-e93014-d1e123.summary: First objection: this seems contrary to the earlier conclusion that faith does not grow in the quantity of articles.

alalal-e93014-d1e133.summary: Second: by what is the number of these quantities of faith determined?

alalal-e93014-d1e140.summary: Third: is faith equally great in all articles? It seems not, since articles of the divinity concern something greater than those of the humanity.

alalal-e93014-d1e164.summary: Further: something handed down that is not an article is the greatest and hardest to believe, Christ's body by transubstantiation of bread and wine; so faith's greatness extends to things joined to the articles.

alalal-e93014-d1e184.summary: Asks further: if Christ's body on the altar is not an article, under which article is it contained as an adjunct?

alalal-e93014-d1e195.summary: First proposal: under omnipotence making all things, as Ambrose argues that the word of Christ, who created all from nothing, can convert bread into his body.

alalal-e93014-d1e215.summary: Second proposal: under the article of the passion, since 1 Corinthians 11:26 says eating this bread proclaims the Lord's death and Luke 22:19 says 'do this in memory of me'.
concepts: Eucharist as memorial of the passion

alalal-e93014-d1e236.summary: Third proposal: under the holy catholic Church and communion of saints, since bread gathered from many grains signifies the unity of the Church (Paul, Augustine), and it is called communion or synaxis.

alalal-e93014-d1e263.summary: Solution: the 'quantity of articles' here means not a number that grows or diminishes but the greatness of dignity each has because first truth underlies it; and Lombard does not say faith grows in all these, but shows in which it grows and in which not.
claims: The greatness of faith in its articles refers to their dignity from first truth, not their number.

alalal-e93014-d1e287.summary: Reply to the second: the dimensions are taken from four aspects of faith. In itself it is great by the quantity of its articles, which contain only what is honourable, true and divine, unlike the laws of other nations that believe shameful, false and demonic things. In the believer it is in the heart and in confession (Romans 10:10): in the heart it grows in intellect by cognition and in affect by devotion; in confession by constancy in preaching and boldness before kings and princes.
claims: Faith is great in its articles, which are wholly honourable, true and divine, and grows in cognition, devotion and confession.

alalal-e93014-d1e329.summary: Reply to the third: regarding the subject of the articles, the motive for believing and the end, all first truth, faith is equal in all articles; but regarding what diversifies them, the connoted way truth is expressed, it is not equal, both because some are expressed in worthier terms and because some conflict less with reason, so faith is greater in believing God three and one than in believing God one.
claims: Faith is equal across articles in its subject, motive and end, but greater in articles that are worthier or more contrary to reason.

alalal-e93014-d1e368.summary: Reply on the Eucharist: Christ's body on the altar, made from bread and wine, is joined to the passion, since the same victim is now offered that was then offered, and the memory of what was done once for all is repeated.
claims: The real presence belongs under the article of the passion, since the same victim is offered.

alalal-e93014-d1e386.summary: Reply on omnipotence: omnipotence is in a way the proof of all the articles, as the angel proved the incarnation to the Virgin, 'no word is impossible with God'; so that objection does not conclude.

alalal-e93014-d1e411.summary: Reply on communion: the communion of saints is the effect of this sacrament, not an article to which it is joined; it is called communion because the sacrament resembles what it causes.

alalal-e93014.summary: Article 5 explains Lombard's statement that faith is great in several respects, without contradicting the earlier conclusion that articles do not grow in number. The 'quantity' of the articles is their dignity from first truth. Faith is great in itself because its articles are wholly honourable, true and divine, unlike the beliefs of other peoples. In the believer it grows in cognition, in devotion and in bold confession. Faith is equal across articles in subject, motive and end, all of which are first truth. It is unequal in how the articles express that truth: greater in worthier articles and in those more contrary to reason, such as the Trinity compared with God's unity. The real presence, which is not itself an article, belongs under the article of the passion, since the same victim is offered. Omnipotence is in a way the proof of all the articles, and the communion of saints is the sacrament's effect.
claims: The greatness of faith in its articles refers to their dignity from first truth, not their number.
Faith is equal across articles in subject, motive and end, but greater in articles worthier or more contrary to reason.
The real presence in the Eucharist belongs under the article of the passion.
